doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

chapter: Founding the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band
title: Bringing the band to Hamilton and why he does it
summary: He drove four band members from New York to Hamilton, and says orthodontics was not enough; he needed to connect to jazz.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. Well let’s talk about some of the things you’ve done. I just watching you today, okay I should tell the people that might be watching this that you brought part of the band up to Hamilton.
Yeah. And did they come from New York?
So you went to New York.

I picked up Zeke on the east side uptown, Jackie Williams on the west side downtown, and then around the corner pretty much is Joey, then I went up to the Bronx and picked up, actually on the Deegan, he’s off the Deegan and we got back on the Deegan in order to come up here. So it was logical but still, I left the house at 9 and we weren’t on our way until 11:30.

Yeah. And it’s twelve hours later. So this is just — so I sort of I’ve done this kind of thing but I was worried about you guys today. Just hoping okay, the trip goes — then I thought about the fact that you’ve taken the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band like to various parts in the world, so not that this is easy today but compared to the logistics that you have handled over the years, I’m amazed and I appreciate the fact that you do it.

Well I do it for myself as well. You know orthodontics wasn’t enough. I needed to be connected to the arts and to music particularly and to jazz very specifically. Because that was what electrified me as a teenager.
So you are able to keep it alive.
Yeah. Luckily I’m healthy. I mean I played soccer at Hamilton. I was an All-American honorable mention for all New York State so physically I’m in good shape, and I can do this.
